newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia's JAT forms charter carriers-agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia's JAT forms charter carriers-agency.

text.p: Yugoslavia's flag carrier JAT Yugoslav Airlines (JAT) said on Monday it will form three charter operators, Tanjug news agency reported on Monday.

Air Yugoslavia will be based in Belgrade, Air Pristina in the capital of the province of Kosovo, and Air Budva in the republic of Montenegro, which together with Serbia makes up the new Yugoslav federation.
Aircraft will be leased from JAT and fly in the colours of the new companies.

JAT is working hard to boost the utilisation of its fleet, affected badly by a market that has shrunk by two thirds after the break-up of former Yugoslavia and by international curbs on intercontinental flights.

Kosovo is a particulary lucrative market for JAT, where it faces competition from a number of Swiss and other European non-scheduled carriers, while Montenegro hopes to woo back Adriatic-coast holidaymakers.
Air Yugoslavia already exists as a subsidiary of JAT, but has so far flown planes in JAT's own colours.
JAT plans to restructure and privatise parts of the new holding company by the year 2000 in an attempt to boost efficiency and profits.
